blocks.text: Re: Engagement for a media relations program
Dear Sandra:

Thank you for the time you and your colleagues have given us over the past several weeks, and for the candor with which you described how Kirby-Taylor is covered today. This letter confirms the terms on which Ashcombe Advisory Partners LLC ("Ashcombe" or "we") will provide a program of media relations to {{fact:f:E-2022-001.client}} (the "Company"). We have tried to record the work as we discussed it, and if any part of this letter differs from your understanding, we would ask you to tell us before you sign.
Purpose and scope

Our shared objective is that the reporters who follow the Company's sector describe it accurately and consistently, and that its spokespeople are well prepared when those reporters call. We propose to pursue that objective through planned and regular contact with the press over the term of the engagement.
Subject to the Company's review and approval at each stage, we expect the program to comprise the following:

items: a review of the Company's recent coverage in print, online, and social channels, which will serve as the baseline against which the program is measured;

a core set of press materials, including a company backgrounder, a fact sheet, and biographies of the Company's designated spokespeople, drawn only from information the Company has already made public or has approved for release;
a list of target reporters and outlets, organized by beat, together with the story angles we propose to offer each of them;
proactive outreach to those reporters, and the arrangement of the interviews and briefings that follow from it;
a preparation session for each spokesperson before a first interview, and a short briefing note ahead of every interview thereafter; and
a protocol for handling inbound media inquiries, with a regular written summary of our outreach and of the coverage that results.

blocks.text: Support for a financing, a transaction, a crisis, or another unplanned announcement is not included in this scope. We would be pleased to discuss any such work separately, and we will not undertake it without your written agreement.
Our approach

We will work through you as the Company's principal contact. Each pitch, statement, and set of talking points will reach you in draft, with a version label and a plain statement of what we are asking you to approve, and nothing will be offered to a reporter on the Company's behalf until you or your designee has approved it in writing.

Media relations for a company with investors to consider calls for particular care. We will take care that nothing we place with the press runs ahead of what the Company has disclosed publicly, and we will consult your finance and legal colleagues wherever a story touches on results, outlook, or a pending matter.
The Ashcombe team

Michael Morris, a Partner of the firm, will hold senior responsibility for the program and will review the press materials and the outreach plan before they are sent to you. Laura Bradley, a Senior Associate, will lead the work from day to day and will be your first point of contact for drafts, approvals, and scheduling.

Kimberly Le, a Communications Analyst, will monitor the Company's coverage and prepare the briefing notes your spokespeople receive before each interview. Melissa Zimmerman, also a Communications Analyst, will develop the background research and peer comparisons on which our story angles depend, and will check each draft against what the Company has already said in public.
I will remain close to the engagement and will read the principal materials before they are released. Should we wish to involve any other member of the firm, we will let you know in advance.
Fee and commencement

Our fee for the program described in this letter is {{fact:f:E-2022-001.fee}}. That fee covers the full scope set out above and will change only if we agree with you in writing to change the scope. The engagement will commence on {{fact:f:E-2022-001.start}}.
Invoicing and payment

We will invoice the fee in monthly installments over the term of the engagement, and each invoice is payable within thirty days of its date. Out-of-pocket expenses, such as media monitoring services, newswire distribution, or travel to an interview, will be billed at cost and incurred only with your prior approval.
Term and termination

We expect the program to run for approximately four months from commencement, and this letter will govern the engagement for that period and for any extension we agree in writing. Either party may end the engagement at any time by written notice to the other.

If the engagement ends before the program is complete, the Company will pay for services performed and approved expenses incurred through the date of termination, and we will deliver all work then in progress. The provisions of this letter on confidentiality and limitation of liability will survive its termination.
Confidentiality

We will hold in confidence all non-public information the Company provides to us, use it solely for this engagement, and share it only with those members of our staff who need it for the work. Each member of the team is bound by the firm's policy on material non-public information and on personal dealing in the securities of clients.

These obligations do not extend to information that is or becomes public other than through us, or that we are required by law to disclose; where the law permits, we will notify you before any such disclosure. We advise other companies, and we will not use the Company's confidential information in that work.
Limitation of liability

The Company is responsible for the accuracy of the information it gives us and for its own decisions about what it releases. We will perform our services with the care customary in our profession; we cannot, however, guarantee that any reporter will cover the Company, nor can we control what is ultimately published.

Our aggregate liability arising out of this engagement will not exceed the fees paid to us under this letter, and neither party will be liable to the other for indirect, incidental, or consequential damages.
Governing law

This letter is governed by the laws of the state in which Ashcombe maintains its principal office, without regard to that state's conflict-of-laws rules. It constitutes the entire agreement between us on its subject and may be amended only in a writing signed by both parties.
Confirming the arrangement

We look forward to working with you and your colleagues at Kirby-Taylor. If these terms are acceptable, please sign below and return a copy to me, and Laura Bradley will then contact you to arrange our first working session.
With kind regards,
Accepted and agreed on behalf of {{fact:f:E-2022-001.client}}:
Kickoff: Kirby-Taylor media relations program

To: Michael Morris; Kimberly Le; Melissa Zimmerman
From: Laura Bradley
Re: How we will run the {{fact:f:E-2022-001.client}} program
Where we are starting
We are under way. The media relations program for {{fact:f:E-2022-001.client}} opened on {{fact:f:E-2022-001.start}}, and the countersigned letter is in the engagement folder.

By the end of the engagement, Kirby-Taylor should have press materials it trusts, a working relationship with the reporters who cover its sector, and spokespeople who are at ease taking their calls. The early weeks are for listening and preparation. We pitch nothing until the materials are approved.

Sandra Mcdaniel, Director of Operations, is our contact at the client. She approves everything before it goes out, and she has asked for one consolidated draft at a time. We will hold ourselves to that.
Five strands of work
The strands overlap. The first two feed everything after them, so they start now.

items: Coverage baseline, Kimberly Le. A review of how the company has been covered in print, online, and on social channels, with daily monitoring running from the first week. This is the yardstick we will report against.

Background and benchmarking, Melissa Zimmerman. How peer companies are covered, which reporters write about the sector, and a fact base built from what the company has already said in public. Every pitch has to agree with it.
Press materials, Laura Bradley. Backgrounder, fact sheet, and spokesperson biographies, drafted from the baseline and the fact base, then taken through Sandra's approval.
Reporter list and outreach, Laura Bradley with Kimberly Le. Targets by beat, the angle we would offer each one, and an outreach schedule once the materials are signed off.
Spokesperson preparation, Michael Morris. A session with each executive before any interview is booked, supported by the briefing notes Kimberly prepares ahead of each call.

blocks.text: Approvals and review

Every draft goes to the client with a version label and one line stating what we are asking Sandra to approve. I will keep the approval log. If you are unsure whether something has been signed off, ask me before it goes anywhere.
Michael Morris will see the press materials and the outreach plan before either reaches the client. Status goes to Sandra on a single email thread, so the record of decisions stays in one place.

The disclosure point in the engagement letter applies to all of us. Nothing we offer a reporter may run ahead of what the company has said publicly. Melissa's fact base is our check on that, so if a pitch needs a figure or a claim that is not in it, come to me before drafting.
We will meet as a team once a week to go through the approval log and the latest coverage. I will send a standing calendar hold.
For this week

items: Kimberly: set up monitoring on the company and its senior executives, and send round a first read of recent coverage.
Melissa: begin the peer coverage comparison, and gather the company's public statements from the past year into one document.
Michael: let me know when you could hold the first preparation sessions, so I can offer dates to the client.
Me: send Sandra our request for existing materials and spokesperson names, and set up the approval log in the folder.

blocks.text: The materials request comes first, because the baseline and the fact base both depend on it. Please send me anything you would like added to it early this week. It goes to Sandra as soon as I have your additions.
Hi Sandra,

The program is on schedule, and the first round of outreach is now within reach. I am opening this thread so that status, questions, and approvals for the {{fact:f:E-2022-001.client}} media work all sit in one place.

Here is where things stand. The coverage review is finished, and daily monitoring has been running since the start of the engagement. The backgrounder and fact sheet are in second draft, with your team's comments folded in. The reporter list is grouped by beat, with a proposed angle beside each name.
Nothing in the recent coverage of Kirby-Taylor calls for a response at this point. If that changes, I will flag it here first.

To keep to schedule, there are a couple of points where we need your help. Could you confirm which executives will speak for the company, and roughly when each could spare time for a preparation session over the next few weeks? And could you let us know whether pitches need sign-off from anyone besides you? I would like to route each draft correctly from the first one.

Best,
Laura
Hi Sandra,

Building on Laura's note, and because the preparation sessions are the one part of the schedule that depends on your executives' calendars and not on ours, I wanted to set out how we would like to run them before you begin asking people for their time:

1. Each spokesperson should complete a session before any interview is booked for them, and we can hold it at your offices or by video, whichever suits the people involved.
2. A session runs about half a day and covers the core messages for Kirby-Taylor, practice interviews built around the questions reporters are most likely to ask, and the subjects we recommend leaving to the company's formal disclosures.
3. If an executive cannot find the time before the first round of outreach, we will leave that person out of it and bring them into a later round once their session has been held.

If you can send us the names and a rough sense of availability by the middle of next week, Laura will propose dates on this thread, and we will fit the outreach schedule for {{fact:f:E-2022-001.client}} around whatever you confirm.

Sincerely,
Michael
Hi Sandra,

Thank you for the quick answers on the phone this morning. We now have the spokesperson names, and your confirmation that Kirby-Taylor pitches come to you alone for sign-off. I have set up our approvals that way.

To be exact about what is with you now: the backgrounder (v3), the fact sheet (v2), and the reporter list (v2). Each reflects the latest comments from your team. Nothing goes to a reporter until all three are approved.

If we can have your approval or your edits by Friday, outreach for {{fact:f:E-2022-001.client}} can begin the following week. Michael's preparation sessions would run alongside it, ahead of any interviews the outreach brings in.

Best,
Laura
Hi Sandra,

Thank you for approving the backgrounder, the fact sheet, and the reporter list, which means the first round of outreach on behalf of {{fact:f:E-2022-001.client}} can begin early next week as planned. Because the work now moves from preparation into direct contact with reporters, I want to confirm how the coming weeks will run:

1. Laura will send you each pitch in its final form before it goes out, so that you see exactly what every reporter receives, even though the materials behind it are already approved.
2. No interview will be confirmed for an executive until that person's preparation session has been held, and we will agree the session dates with you on this thread.
3. Starting at the end of the first week of outreach, we will send you a short weekly summary of the reporters contacted, the responses received, and any coverage that results, together with anything from our monitoring that deserves your attention.
In the meantime, if a reporter contacts anyone at Kirby-Taylor directly, please pass the inquiry to Laura or to me, so that what the caller hears matches what we are offering in the outreach.

Sincerely,
Michael
